questions.question: Which of the following new digital facilities was launched in May 2025 by the Union Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment during the ‘Ageing with Dignity’ event?

options.text: Employment Exchange Portal for Senior Citizens

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Senior Citizens Welfare Portal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Union Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment** launched the **Senior Citizens Welfare Portal** during the **‘Ageing with Dignity’ event** held in **May 2025**.
 
• The portal was developed to address the growing needs of India’s **elderly population**, ensuring their access to **welfare services**, **healthcare**, and **social support systems**.
 
• This digital initiative aims to create a centralized platform for **senior citizens** to avail various government schemes and services efficiently.
 
• The portal also includes features like **helpline services**, **financial assistance tools**, and **information dissemination** to empower senior citizens and improve their quality of life.
 
• The launch of this portal aligns with the government’s commitment to promoting **age-inclusive policies** and ensuring the dignity, security, and welfare of the elderly.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **India’s Ageing Population:**

 
 
• As per the **Census 2011**, India has around **104 million senior citizens**, with this number expected to increase significantly by **2050**.
 
• The country faces challenges in providing adequate **healthcare**, **financial security**, and **social engagement** for its ageing population.
 
 
 
• **Government Initiatives for Senior Citizens:**
 
 
• The **Integrated Programme for Senior Citizens (IPSrC)** provides financial assistance to NGOs for running **elderly care homes** and day-care centers.
 
• The **Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana** distributes physical aids and assistive devices to senior citizens belonging to **below poverty line (BPL)** families.
 
• The **Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007** ensures legal protection for elderly individuals against neglect and abuse.
 
 
 
• **Digital Initiatives for Senior Citizens:**
 
 
• Digital platforms like the Senior Citizens Welfare Portal aim to bridge the gap between technology and elderly care.
 
• These platforms provide access to **healthcare services**, **financial planning tools**, and **social interaction opportunities**, fostering independence among senior citizens.
 
 
 
• **Employment Exchange Portal for Senior Citizens:**
 
 
• This portal facilitates the re-employment of senior citizens in various sectors, utilizing their experience and expertise.
 
• It is particularly beneficial for retired professionals seeking to contribute to the workforce or engage in part-time employment.
 
 
 
• **Digital Life Certificate Platform:**
 
 
• Launched under the **Jeevan Pramaan initiative**, this platform enables pensioners to submit their life certificates online without visiting banks or government offices.
 
• It uses biometric authentication to ensure security and ease of use for senior citizens.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Features of Senior Citizens Welfare Portal:**

 
 
• Centralized access to **government schemes** and **welfare programs**.
 
• Integration with helpline services for **emergency assistance** and **counseling support**.
 
• Dedicated sections for **financial planning**, **healthcare resources**, and **legal aid**.
 
• Regular updates on **policy changes** and **new initiatives** for senior citizens.
 
 
 
• **Global Trends in Elderly Care:**
 
 
• Countries like **Japan** and **Sweden** have implemented advanced technologies like **robotic caregivers** and **smart homes** for elderly care.
 
• India is gradually adopting similar digital solutions to address challenges related to its ageing population.

questions.question: India set a new Guinness World Record in 2025 for the largest human formation of which of the following symbols?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ashoka Chakra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• India set a new **Guinness World Record in 2025** for the largest human formation of the **Ashoka Chakra**, a symbol of peace, dharma, and progress.
 
• The event took place with the participation of thousands of people who came together to form the intricate design of the **Ashoka Chakra**, which is featured prominently on the Indian national flag.
 
• The **Ashoka Chakra** consists of 24 spokes, representing the 24 virtues such as love, courage, patience, and righteousness, which are significant in Indian cultural and philosophical heritage.
 
• This record-breaking event was organized to promote unity, patriotism, and the values that the **Ashoka Chakra** symbolizes in Indian society.
 
• The Guinness World Record team verified the formation's accuracy and adherence to the dimensions of the **Ashoka Chakra** as depicted on the national flag.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Ashoka Chakra:**

 
 
• The **Ashoka Chakra** is derived from the Lion Capital of Ashoka at Sarnath, which is one of the most prominent symbols of India's rich heritage.
 
• It represents the **wheel of dharma**, embodying the principles of truth, justice, and progress.
 
• The 24 spokes in the chakra symbolize the life cycle and virtues essential for maintaining harmony and balance.
 
• It is prominently displayed in the center of the **Indian national flag**, signifying motion and dynamism.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Guinness World Records:**
 
 
• Guinness World Records is an internationally recognized authority for documenting extraordinary feats and achievements.
 
• India has consistently set records in various domains, showcasing its cultural, social, and scientific achievements.
 
• Events like the formation of the **Ashoka Chakra** highlight the nation's unity and collective spirit.
 
 
 
• **Other Notable Symbols:**
 
 
• **Heart Shape:** Globally recognized as a symbol of love and compassion.
 
• **Olympic Rings:** Representing the unity of five continents and the Olympic spirit.
 
• **Peace Symbol:** Widely used to signify harmony and the absence of conflict.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context of the Ashoka Chakra:**
 
 
• The chakra is named after **Emperor Ashoka**, one of India's greatest rulers, who embraced Buddhism and propagated values of peace and dharma.
 
• It is a reminder of India's commitment to universal values and moral principles.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Guinness World Record Verification:**

 
 
• The record-breaking formation required precise planning and execution to accurately depict the **Ashoka Chakra**.
 
• Participants were trained to understand the design and significance of the symbol.
 
• Such events foster patriotism and are a celebration of India's national identity.
 
 
 
• **Role of Symbols in National Identity:**
 
 
• Symbols like the **Ashoka Chakra** play a pivotal role in expressing the ethos and values of a nation.
 
• They are used in national events, government documents, and cultural representations.
 
• Educational programs often emphasize their importance to instill respect and pride in citizens.

questions.question: Which sport had the most Arjuna Award recipients in January 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Para-Athletics**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Para-Athletics** had the most recipients of the **Arjuna Awards** in January 2025, recognizing the exceptional achievements of Indian athletes with disabilities in various sports disciplines.
 
• The **Arjuna Award** is one of India's most prestigious national sports honors, aimed at acknowledging outstanding performance in sports and games.
 
• A significant number of **Para-Athletes** received the Arjuna Award due to their remarkable contributions, including medals in international competitions such as the **Paralympics** and World Para-Athletics Championships.
 
• The increased recognition for Para-Athletics showcases India's focus on promoting **inclusive sports culture** and supporting athletes with disabilities.
 
• Prominent awardees include athletes excelling in events like **track and field, wheelchair sports, and powerlifting**, among others, making Para-Athletics the leading category in terms of awardees.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Arjuna Award:**

 
 
• Established in **1961**, the Arjuna Award honors excellence in sports and is conferred by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, Government of India.
 
• Recipients are selected based on their performance at **national and international levels**, as well as their ability to inspire others through sports.
 
• The award includes a **bronze statuette of Arjuna**, a certificate, and a cash prize.
 
• It recognizes achievements in both **Olympic and Paralympic sports**, as well as indigenous and non-Olympic sports.
 
 
 
• **Para-Athletics:**
 
 
• Para-Athletics is a category of sports designed for athletes with physical disabilities, featuring events like **running, jumping, throwing, and wheelchair racing**.
 
• India has made significant strides in Para-Athletics, with athletes like **Devendra Jhajharia** and **Mariyappan Thangavelu** achieving global recognition.
 
• The **Paralympic Games** serve as the pinnacle event for Para-Athletes, offering opportunities to compete at the highest level.
 
• India's Para-Athletes have brought home numerous medals from events like the **Tokyo 2020 Paralympics**, boosting awareness and support for disabled athletes.
 
 
 
• **Inclusive Sports Initiatives:**
 
 
• The Government of India has launched several schemes to promote sports among disabled individuals, such as the **Khelo India Programme**.
 
• Specialized training centers and funding mechanisms have been established to provide **world-class facilities** and support for Para-Athletes.
 
• Programs like **Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS)** have been extended to Para-Athletes, ensuring they receive adequate financial and coaching support.
 
 
 
• **Other Sports Categories:**
 
 
• **Hockey:** Historically a popular category for Arjuna Award recipients due to India’s legacy in international hockey tournaments.
 
• **Athletics:** Covers track and field events, with awardees often excelling in international competitions like the Olympics and Asian Games.
 
• **Shooting:** A high-achieving category where Indian shooters have won multiple medals in events like the Olympics and Commonwealth Games.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Recognition for Para-Athletes:**

 
 
• Para-Athletes receiving the Arjuna Award signifies growing support for inclusive sports.
 
• India’s performance in Para-Athletics on global platforms has led to increased acknowledgment and funding opportunities.
 
• These awards encourage more disabled individuals to pursue sports professionally.
 
 
 
• **Role of Government:**
 
 
• Various government schemes, including the **National Sports Development Fund**, aim to support athletes with disabilities.
 
• The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports ensures that Para-Athletes have access to **modern equipment, training, and coaching facilities**.
 
• Government recognition through awards like Arjuna highlights the importance of fostering an inclusive environment in sports.

questions.question: As announced by the Government of India, as on 7 July 2025, how many biotech startups does India have, compared to just 50 a decade ago?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nearly 11,000**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• As of **7 July 2025**, India has nearly **11,000 biotech startups**, according to the Government of India. This marks a significant growth from just **50 biotech startups a decade ago (2015)**.
 
• The biotech industry in India has been growing at a rapid pace due to increased **government initiatives, funding, and policy support** aimed at fostering innovation and entrepreneurship in the sector.
 
• India's biotech sector is supported by initiatives like **Make in India** and **Startup India**, which encourage innovation in fields such as **healthcare, agriculture, bioinformatics, and industrial biotechnology**.
 
• The country is now among the top 12 biotech destinations globally and ranks **third in the Asia-Pacific region**.
 
• The establishment of biotech parks, incubators, and research institutions, coupled with government schemes, has created a **favorable ecosystem for startups** in the biotechnology domain.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Biotechnology Industry in India:**

 
 
• The Indian biotechnology industry is valued at approximately **$100 billion**, with projections to grow exponentially in the coming years.
 
• It is divided into five major segments: **biopharma, bioagriculture, bioindustry, bioinformatics, and bioservices**.
 
• India is one of the largest producers of vaccines in the world and is a major exporter of generic medicines and biopharmaceuticals.
 
 
 
• **Government Initiatives for Biotech Growth:**
 
 
• **Biotechnology Industry Research Assistance Council (BIRAC)**: A public sector enterprise that promotes innovation and entrepreneurship in the biotech industry by providing financial and infrastructural support.
 
• **National Biotechnology Development Strategy**: Aims to establish India as a global hub for biotechnology innovation and manufacturing by promoting research and entrepreneurship.
 
• **Startup India Initiative**: Provides funding, mentoring, and incubation support to startups, including those in biotechnology.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Biotechnology:**
 
 
• Used in healthcare for **drug development, gene therapy, and diagnostics**.
 
• Plays a vital role in agriculture through **genetically modified crops** and **biofertilizers**.
 
• Contributes to industrial applications such as **bioplastics, biofuels**, and **environmental conservation**.
 
 
 
• **Global Standing of Indian Biotechnology:**
 
 
• India ranks among the **top 12 biotech destinations globally** and is recognized for its **affordable innovation**.
 
• Major Indian biotech companies include **Biocon, Serum Institute of India, Panacea Biotech**, and **Dr. Reddy’s Laboratories**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Biotech Parks in India:**

 
 
• India has established numerous biotech parks, including **Genome Valley in Hyderabad**, the **Biotech Park in Lucknow**, and the **Biotechnology City in Bangalore**, to promote research, development, and entrepreneurship.
 
• These parks provide **state-of-the-art infrastructure, R&D facilities, and funding** opportunities for startups and researchers.
 
 
 
• **Key Challenges in Biotech Sector:**
 
 
• Lack of sufficient funding for early-stage startups and **high R&D costs**.
 
• Stringent regulatory policies and **intellectual property issues** pose significant hurdles.
 
• Limited availability of skilled manpower in niche areas of biotechnology.

questions.question: Which state became the third Indian state to be recognised as fully functionally literate, under the ULLAS – New India Literacy Programme, in June 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tripura**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tripura** became the third Indian state to achieve the status of being fully functionally literate under the **ULLAS – New India Literacy Programme** in June 2025.
 
• The state achieved functional literacy by ensuring that all individuals above the age of 15 could read, write, and perform basic arithmetic operations, a significant milestone in improving education accessibility.
 
• The **ULLAS – New India Literacy Programme** aims to provide universal functional literacy and numeracy to individuals in the age group of 15 and above who missed the opportunity for formal schooling.
 
• Tripura follows the path of two other states, **Kerala** and **Bihar**, which were earlier recognized as fully functionally literate states.
 
• The initiative was implemented with the active participation of teachers, volunteers, and community members, which significantly contributed to the state’s success.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **ULLAS – New India Literacy Programme:**

 
 
• ULLAS stands for **Understanding Lifelong Learning for All in Society** and is an initiative by the Government of India to eradicate adult illiteracy.
 
• It targets individuals aged 15 and above who were unable to complete formal education, focusing on **basic literacy, numeracy, and life skills**.
 
• The program uses innovative teaching methods, including digital platforms, for effective outreach and participation.
 
• ULLAS aligns with the broader goals of **Sustainable Development Goal 4 (SDG 4)** – Quality Education, ensuring inclusive and equitable education for all.
 
 
 
• **Functional Literacy:**
 
 
• Functional literacy refers to the ability of an individual to read, write, and perform basic arithmetic operations necessary for day-to-day functioning and economic participation.
 
• This includes skills such as filling out forms, reading labels, and performing calculations like budgeting and financial transactions.
 
• Achieving functional literacy is considered a crucial step toward reducing poverty and enhancing individual empowerment.
 
 
 
• **Tripura’s Literacy Achievements:**
 
 
• Tripura has consistently performed well in literacy indicators, with a literacy rate of over **87%** (as per the 2011 Census).
 
• The state’s government has implemented numerous literacy campaigns, including adult education programs, to ensure inclusive educational development.
 
 
 
• **Kerala’s Functional Literacy:**
 
 
• **Kerala** was the first Indian state to achieve complete literacy in **1991** and continues to lead in educational advancements.
 
• The state emphasizes universal education access, with significant investments in public education and teacher training programs.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Government Initiatives to Promote Literacy:**

 
 
• **Saakshar Bharat:** A Government of India program launched in **2009** to promote adult literacy, especially among women and marginalized groups.
 
• **National Literacy Mission (NLM):** Established in **1988**, the NLM aims to eradicate illiteracy among adults aged 15 and above by promoting voluntary literacy campaigns.
 
• **Digital Literacy Campaigns:** Efforts to enhance digital literacy among rural populations, such as the **Pradhan Mantri Gramin Digital Saksharta Abhiyan (PMGDISHA).**
 
 
 
• **Global Context:**
 
 
• According to the **UNESCO Institute for Statistics**, approximately **773 million adults worldwide** lack basic literacy skills as of 2023.
 
• India’s literacy initiatives contribute significantly to global efforts to achieve **universal literacy** under SDG 4.

questions.question: Where did the chemical factory blast occur on 30 June 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sangareddy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The chemical factory blast on **30 June 2025** occurred in **Sangareddy**, a district in the Indian state of **Telangana**.
 
• **Sangareddy** is known for its industrial setup, including pharmaceutical and chemical factories, which may pose risks due to mishandling of chemicals or technical failures.
 
• Such incidents in industrial areas highlight the importance of **stringent safety protocols** and regular audits to prevent accidents.
 
• The blast led to significant damage in the vicinity and raised concerns about **industrial safety standards** in the region.
 
• Authorities initiated an investigation to determine the cause of the explosion, which could include factors like **chemical reactions, equipment failure, or human error**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sangareddy District:**

 
 
• Sangareddy is located in the Indian state of **Telangana** and serves as a hub for various industries, particularly in the sectors of **pharmaceuticals**, chemicals, and manufacturing.
 
• It is situated close to the state capital, **Hyderabad**, making it a strategic location for industrial development.
 
• The district also houses the **Patencheru Industrial Area**, which is one of the major industrial zones in Telangana.
 
 
 
• **Industrial Accidents:**
 
 
• Industrial accidents occur due to factors like **negligence in safety measures, equipment failure, improper handling of chemicals**, or lack of training for workers.
 
• Such incidents may lead to **loss of lives, injuries, property damage**, and environmental degradation.
 
• They highlight the need for stringent enforcement of **Occupational Safety and Health (OSH)** regulations.
 
 
 
• **Safety Measures in Chemical Factories:**
 
 
• Regular inspection and maintenance of machinery and equipment are crucial to prevent technical failures.
 
• Implementation of **Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs)** and training for workers to handle hazardous materials safely.
 
• Proper storage and labeling of chemicals to avoid accidents due to incorrect handling.
 
• Emergency response systems, including **firefighting equipment**, evacuation plans, and medical facilities, are essential to mitigate the impact of accidents.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Industrial Accidents:**
 
 
• The **Bhopal Gas Tragedy** in 1984 is one of the most infamous industrial disasters, caused by the leakage of **methyl isocyanate** from a pesticide plant in Madhya Pradesh.
 
• The **Visakhapatnam Gas Leak** in 2020 involved the leakage of **styrene gas** from a chemical plant, causing deaths and health issues.
 
• Such incidents emphasize the importance of learning from past failures and implementing preventive measures.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Legal Framework:**

 
 
• The **Factories Act of 1948** governs the safety, health, and welfare of workers in factories in India.
 
• It mandates employers to provide proper **safety equipment, training**, and emergency response mechanisms.
 
• Failure to comply with safety regulations can lead to **legal penalties** and closure of operations.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Impact:**
 
 
• Chemical blasts can result in **air and water pollution**, affecting nearby communities and ecosystems.
 
• Proper disposal and containment of hazardous waste are necessary to minimize long-term environmental damage.
 
 
 
• **Government Initiatives:**
 
 
• The **National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA)** provides guidelines for managing industrial disasters and mitigating risks.
 
• State governments often collaborate with industries to conduct safety audits and ensure compliance with regulations.

questions.question: In 2025, which city in Maharashtra has achieved 100% segregation, collection and processing of sanitary and biomedical waste, handling an average of 300 to 350 kg of sanitary waste daily?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Karad**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Karad**, a city in Maharashtra, achieved **100% segregation, collection, and processing** of sanitary and biomedical waste by 2025.
 
• The city successfully handles an average of **300 to 350 kg of sanitary waste daily**, showcasing its commitment to efficient waste management practices.
 
• This achievement is a result of strict implementation of waste segregation at the source, supported by awareness campaigns and cooperation from citizens.
 
• The sanitary and biomedical waste is processed using advanced methods, ensuring eco-friendly disposal and minimizing environmental impact.
 
• This milestone places Karad as a model city for waste management practices, inspiring other cities in Maharashtra and India to follow suit.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Biomedical Waste Management:**

 
 
• Biomedical waste includes **infectious and hazardous materials** generated during medical and healthcare activities.
 
• According to the **Biomedical Waste Management Rules, 2016**, proper segregation, treatment, and disposal are mandatory to prevent contamination.
 
• Methods of disposal include **incineration, autoclaving, and chemical disinfection**.
 
 
 
• **Sanitary Waste Management:**
 
 
• Sanitary waste refers to used personal hygiene products like **sanitary napkins, diapers, and tampons**.
 
• Improper disposal of sanitary waste can lead to health hazards and environmental pollution.
 
• Innovative techniques such as **composting and incineration** are employed to manage sanitary waste effectively.
 
 
 
• **Waste Management Initiatives in India:**
 
 
• The **Swachh Bharat Abhiyan**, launched in 2014, aimed to achieve universal sanitation and waste management across India.
 
• The **Solid Waste Management Rules, 2016**, focus on segregation, recycling, and disposal of solid waste.
 
• Several cities, including Indore, Surat, and Karad, have been recognized for their efficient waste management systems.
 
 
 
• **Role of Technology in Waste Management:**
 
 
• Technologies like **GPS-enabled tracking** for waste collection vehicles ensure better monitoring and efficiency.

questions.question: On 24 May 2025, the order of which High Court was overturned by the Supreme Court and ruled that denying maternity leave for a third child violates a woman's constitutional right, reinforcing her dignity and reproductive freedom?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Madras High Court**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Supreme Court of India** overturned the order of the **Madras High Court** on **24 May 2025**, ruling that denying maternity leave for a third child is unconstitutional.
 
• This judgment upheld a woman's **constitutional right**, emphasizing her **dignity** and **reproductive freedom**.
 
• The court stated that maternity leave for a third child is crucial for ensuring women's **health** and **well-being**.
 
• The decision aligns with the principles of **gender equality** enshrined in the **Constitution of India**.
 
• This ruling reinforces the importance of **social security measures** for working women, particularly in the context of maternal care.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Constitutional Provisions Related to Maternity Rights:**

 
 
• **Article 14:** Guarantees **equality before the law** and protection against discrimination.
 
• **Article 15:** Prohibits discrimination based on gender, ensuring equal rights for women.
 
• **Article 42:** Directs the state to make provisions for securing **maternity benefits** and ensuring just working conditions.
 
 
 
• **Maternity Benefit Act, 1961:**
 
 
• Under this act, women are entitled to **26 weeks of paid maternity leave** for the first two children.
 
• For the third child, the leave entitlement is limited to **12 weeks**.
 
• The Supreme Court ruling challenges restrictions for third-child maternity leave, promoting equal treatment.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the Ruling:**
 
 
• This decision ensures that women can exercise their reproductive rights without fear of losing employment benefits.
 
• It highlights the importance of **healthcare** and **social security** for working mothers.
 
• The judgment sets a precedent for future cases concerning women's rights and maternity benefits.
 
 
 
• **Other High Courts:**
 
 
• The **Hyderabad High Court**, **Bombay High Court**, and **Allahabad High Court** have also addressed women's rights in various cases.
 
• However, in this instance, the **Madras High Court** ruling was specifically overturned.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Supreme Court Judgment:**

 
 
• The ruling reinforces women's rights to **workplace equality** and **maternity benefits**.
 
• This is a significant development in improving **gender equity** in India.
 
 
 
• **Global Context:**
 
 
• Many countries, including **Sweden** and **Norway**, offer comprehensive maternity leave policies to support working mothers.
 
• The Indian Supreme Court ruling aligns with global efforts to promote **women's empowerment**.

questions.question: Which startup was selected in April 2025 to build India’s first sovereign Indic LLM under the IndiaAI Mission?

• **Indic LLM** refers to a large-scale language model specifically designed to cater to **Indian languages**, ensuring inclusivity for regional and vernacular language users across the nation.

• The mission also focuses on creating **inclusive AI technologies** to bridge the digital divide and cater to the linguistic diversity of India.
 
• It aims to position India as a global leader in the field of Artificial Intelligence through **collaborations between academia, industry, and government institutions**.

• They are used in applications such as **chatbots, machine translation, text summarization, and sentiment analysis**.
 
• Developing Indic LLMs ensures that AI technologies support **India’s linguistic diversity**, including regional languages like **Hindi, Tamil, Bengali, Telugu, and Marathi**.
 
• These models are essential for enhancing accessibility and inclusivity in digital services for **non-English speaking users**.
 
 
 
• **Sarvam AI:**
 
 
• **Sarvam AI** is a leading Indian startup focusing on **AI-driven solutions** for societal and linguistic challenges.
 
• Its expertise lies in developing AI systems that respect **cultural contexts** and address the unique needs of the Indian demographic.
 
• Sarvam AI's approach emphasizes **ethical AI development**, ensuring fairness, inclusivity, and transparency in its solutions.
 
• By being chosen for the IndiaAI Mission, Sarvam AI reinforces its position as a key player in India's AI ecosystem.
 
 
 
• **Other AI Startups:**
 
 
• **Wadhwani AI:** Focuses on AI solutions for **social impact**, particularly in agriculture and healthcare.
 
• **People+AI:** Specializes in developing AI systems that enhance **human productivity** and collaboration.
 
• **AI4 Bharat:** Known for its contributions to **natural language processing (NLP)** and AI research for Indian languages.
 
• While these startups are significant players in the AI domain, **Sarvam AI** was chosen for its expertise in Indic LLM development.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

questions.question: On 16 May 2025, the Supreme Court invalidated the Indian Government's orders passed in which years, allowing ex-post facto environmental clearances?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2017 and 2021**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• On **16 May 2025**, the Supreme Court of India invalidated the **Indian Government’s orders** that were passed in the years **2017 and 2021**. These orders permitted **ex-post facto environmental clearances**.
 
• **Ex-post facto environmental clearance** refers to the practice of granting environmental approval for projects that have already started construction or operation without prior clearance, which is against the provisions of environmental laws.
 
• The Supreme Court ruling stated that such clearances violate the principles of **environmental sustainability** and the requirements laid down under the **Environment (Protection) Act, 1986**.
 
• The judgment emphasized that **environmental clearances** must be obtained before initiating any project that has significant environmental impacts to ensure compliance with environmental protection standards.&

questions.question: As reported in May 2025, the study by Climate Trends, a Delhi-based research consultancy, examined NASA satellite data of the Himalayan glaciers from 2000-2023 to evaluate the impact of which of the following on Himalayan snow?
questions.solution: The correct answer is __**Black Carbon**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** • **Black Carbon** is a type of particulate matter that results from the incomplete combustion of fossil fuels, biofuels, and biomass. • The study by Climate Trends (May 2025) examined **NASA satellite data (2000-2023)** to assess the impact of black carbon on **Himalayan snow and glaciers**. • Black carbon particles settle on snow and ice, reducing their albedo (reflectivity). This causes the snow to absorb more sunlight, leading to faster melting. • The Himalayan region is particularly sensitive to black carbon as it is home to some of the world's largest glaciers, which are a critical water source for millions of people. • The deposition of black carbon in the Himalayas is primarily linked to human activities such as **vehicle emissions, industrial processes, and agricultural burning** in South Asia.
